newsitem.title: DUBAI: SOCCER-GULF FOES SHARE POINTS TO REACH QUARTER-FINALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GULF FOES SHARE POINTS TO REACH QUARTER-FINALS.

text.p: Gulf foes Saudi Arabia, Iran and Iraq finished their group B matches neck-and-neck on Wednesday to move into the quarter finals of the 11th Asian Cup.
Triple champions Iran surprised highly ranked Saudi Arabia with a 3-0 victory and Iraq defeated lowly Thailand 4-1 in Dubai.
The three Gulf sides finished their group matches with six points each.

Iran topped the table by virtue of their 3-0 defeat of Saudi Arabia earlier on Wednesday, the Saudi's qualified in second place and Iraq are guarenteed one of the quarter-final berthes reserved for the two third-placed teams with the greatest numder of points from the three groups.
Thailand finished without a point and go out of the 12-nation competition.

With all group A matches played, hosts the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait have qualified for the knockout stage, with third-placed South Korea having to wait for the results of group C's final matches on Thursday to see if they qualify.

Holders Japan have already ensured a quarter-final berth from group C. China, who plays Japan on Thursday, and Uzbekistan, who face Syria, both have three points from two games. South Korea have four points from three matches.

Backed by some 5,000 supporters waving Iranian flags and chanting Islam's rallying cry of ''Allahu Akbar'' (God is Greatest), Iran were well worth their victory, unexpectedly dominating their match against the highly-fancied Saudis.
Iranian coach Hassan Jahanpour attributed the victory to hard work.
''I'm very happy with this victory...I dedicate this victory to the Iranian people who I know must be very happy,'' he told a post match news conference.
Ties between Sunni Moslem Saudi Arabia and Shi'ite Iran have been tense since the Islamic revolution of 1979 which swept Iran's late leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini to power.
Saudi Arabia backed Iraq in an eight-year war against Iran in the 1980s but then went to war against the Iraqis over Kuwait in 1991.
Iran had a dream start in Wednesday's match when defender Karim Bagheri rocked Saudi Arabia with a goal in the 12th minute.
A corner played into the six-yard box was half cleared by the Saudi defence, allowing Bagheri to control the ball on the penalty spot and drive the ball past keeper Mohammed al- Daeyea.

Khodadad Azizi ran at the Saudi defence from the left and cut the ball back to striker Ali Daei on the edge of the area. Daei, unmarked, took the ball in his stride and unleashed a low drive that beat a diving Daeyea, hit his left post and went in.
Azizi scored a brilliant individual goal himself in the 48th minute, dribbling past three defenders inside the penalty area before slotting the ball home to put Iran 3-0 up.
Iraq strikers Hayder Majeed and Laith Shihaib scored two goals apiece in the defeat of Thailand.
Majeed opened the scoring for Iraq in the 17th minute, tapping in a left flank cross. Six minutes later Shihaib made it two with a low 25-metre drive that beat Wacharapong Somcit on his right post.
Majeed headed in a corner by Shihaib in the 50th minute to restore Iraq's two goal advantage.

Shihaib grabbed his second and Iraq's fourth with the game's best goal in the 65th minute, beating his marker before unleashing a right foot drive from 20-metres into the top corner of Wacharapong's goal.
Dusit Chalerman scored Thailand's consolation goal.
